title: Failure Isolation and Rollback Playbook for Private Deployments
author: Aisha Khan
body:
Summary:

This playbook describes failure isolation patterns, safe rollback procedures, verification checks, and communication steps for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for SREs, Platform engineers, and Customer Success engineers who run day-2 operations or perform upgrades/patches that risk degrading service availability, security posture, or data integrity.

Goals:
- Minimize customer-visible disruption during upgrades and incidents.
- Ensure safe automated and manual rollback paths exist for all control-plane and data-plane changes.
- Provide clear ownership, decision criteria, and verification checks for rollback decisions.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to: Redwood Private control plane, connector agents, inference runtime nodes, KV/cache tiers, and networking changes introduced during patch/upgrade or configuration rollout.
- Does NOT cover: customer-managed external dependencies (e.g., third-party DBs) except where Redwood config changes interact directly.

Preconditions (must-check before any planned upgrade):
1) Backups & snapshots: confirm last full control-plane snapshot is completed and stored in the configured customer bucket. Snapshot timestamp: <ISO timestamp>.
2) Health baseline: capture baseline metrics for 15 min prior to change (latency p95, CPU/GPU utilization, request success rate, cache hit rate). Attach reports to the change ticket.
3) Canary capacity: allocate a canary pool with isolated routing (>=1% traffic and at least N concurrent sessions, where N = max(10, 0.01 * expected concurrent load)).
4) Rollback playbook verified: owners and on-call contact listed in the change ticket.

Key failure-isolation patterns (design rules):
- Traffic fencing: use route-level flags and feature gates so new binaries/configs can be routed only from an explicit routing table entry.
- Config gating: store critical rollout knobs in the control-plane feature collection; changes to these keys must be reversible and have a TTL.
- Immutable artifacts: build deterministic artifacts (sha256). If artifact mismatch occurs, auto-reject rollout.
- Gradual widening: 0 -> canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated health gates at each step.

Decision criteria for rollback (one or more triggers):
- Latency: sustained p95 increase > 2x baseline for 5 minutes.
- Errors: request error rate increase > 1% absolute and >= 3x baseline for 3 minutes.
- Throughput degradation: end-to-end throughput drop > 20% for 5 minutes with no external cause.
- Resource saturation: any node with GPU memory OOM, kernel panic, repeated process restarts (>3 restarts in 5 minutes).
- Security regression: any failing auth or encryption checks during/after rollout.

Recommended manual rollback procedure (control-plane or runtime service):
1) Triage and verify: confirm metrics trigger was real (check Prometheus, traces, and node logs). Record decision in the incident/change ticket.
2) Stop new widening: set rollout flag to paused.
3) Shift traffic: route 100% traffic away from canary/widened group to last-known-good pool. Use routing command: 
   rwd-router set-route --deployment <DEPLOYMENT_ID> --target-pool <GOOD_POOL_ID> --drain-time 30s
4) If traffic cannot be re-routed cleanly, place a temporary denylist for new sessions at the gateway: 
   rwd-gateway denylist add --match "session=new" --reason "rollback in progress"
5) Revert artifacts: pin model/runtime to previous artifact SHA. Example pin file (used by control-plane):

   pinned_artifact: >
     deployment: infra-runtime
     version: 2026.01.14
     sha256: abcd1234ef567890...

   Apply revert command: rwd-deploy rollback --deployment infra-runtime --to-sha abcd1234ef567890 --force

6) Rollback config: restore previous config bundle from snapshot store. Example restore: rwd-config restore --snapshot-id snap-20260210-2145 --components control-plane,runtime
7) Verify service health: follow verification checklist below.
8) Close ticket with a post-rollback summary including root cause hypothesis and actions to mitigate in next rollout.

Automated rollback choreography (when health gates are enabled):
- Health gate engine monitors: p95 latency, error rate, GPU OOM rate, and control-plane heartbeat.
- If any configured gate trips, the system will attempt: 1) pause widen, 2) move traffic back to the last good pool, 3) notify on-call channel, 4) if critical triggers persist for 90s, automatically initiate artifact revert.
- To disable automated rollback for a specific rollout, add hold tag: rollout.hold=true in the change request (not recommended unless supervised).

Verification checklist (post-rollback):
- Control-plane: api-server 200s check, queue depth stable, config hash matches pinned SHA.
- Runtime: no GPU OOMs for 30 minutes, tail latency p50/p95 within 15% of baseline.
- Workloads: 10 synthetic requests per model class succeed end-to-end, embeddings within expected vector L2 tolerance.
- Logs: no new error patterns (>5 occurrences) in last 15 minutes.
- Security: TLS session negotiation passes, KMS sign/verify checks succeed.

Concrete commands and examples (CLI snippets):
- Snapshot control plane:
  rwd-control snapshot create --name pre-upgrade-2026-02-12

- Create canary pool (example YAML passed to control-plane API):
  ```yaml
  kind: Pool
  name: canary-2026-02-12
  labels:
    purpose: canary
    owner: eng-platform
  size: 4
  allowed_models: [rwd-gpt-small, rwd-gpt-medium]
  ```

- Trigger manual rollback for runtime:
  rwd-deploy rollback --deployment inference-runtime --reason "p95 spike" --to-tag last-good

- Inspect recent errors (Kubernetes example):
  kubectl -n rwd-runtime logs deployment/inference-runtime --since=15m | grep -i error | head -n 200

Operational notes and edge cases:
- Database schema incompatible migrations: never auto-rollback schema changes. For schema rollouts, use migration gating and a multi-step backward-compatible migration plan. If a schema incompatibility is detected, trigger service-level rollback but coordinate with DBA team to run the corrective migration.
- Persistent data corruption suspected: isolate affected nodes immediately, take disk snapshots, and contact Security for potential forensics. Do NOT reintroduce those nodes into the pool.
- Multi-region fallbacks: if local region capacity causes rollback, prefer moving traffic to a warm spare region with identical model versions. Ensure legal/data-residency approvals before cross-region movement.

Post-incident actions and ownership:
- Postmortem owner: on-call engineer who initiated rollback (or explicit postmortem owner in ticket).
- RCA timeline: initial report due within 2 business days, full RCA with action items within 7 business days.
- Preventative controls: implement additional health gates, add synthetic tests, or modify resource requests based on root cause.

Compatibility and upgrade matrix (excerpt):
- Control plane version 2025.12.x: compatible with runtime 2025.10.x -> 2026.01.x (recommended).
- Runtime GPU driver: NVIDIA 535.x required for 16-bit quantized kernels.
- KV cache format v2 requires control-plane >=2026.01.

Safety checklist before re-attempting rollout:
1) Confirm root cause has been mitigated or a compensating control exists.
2) Increase canary pool size by 2x and reduce widening step to 5% increments.
3) Add extra synthetic probes and extend observation window to 30 minutes between steps.
4) Ensure on-call rotation for the next 48 hours has explicit coverage.

Troubleshooting quick reference (common scenarios):
- Symptom: p95 doubled immediately after rollout. Check: network egress throttling on gateway, routing misconfiguration, and runtime CPU throttling. Action: move traffic and revert.
- Symptom: GPU OOM on new model. Check: model quantization profile, batch size defaults. Action: rollback to previous model; file model-onboarding ticket.

Appendix A — Minimal set of monitoring queries to attach to the change ticket:
- PromQL p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, route))
- Error rate: sum(rate(request_errors_total[1m])) / sum(rate(request_total[1m]))
- Node restarts: increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[5m]) > 0

Appendix B — Contact & escalation matrix:
- Primary on-call (Platform SRE): pager duty rotation rwd-platform-pager (escalate after 5 min)
- Control-plane owner: eng-platform@redwood.example.com
- Security: sec-ops@redwood.example.com (for suspected compromise)

Document maintenance:
- Owner: eng-platform
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any major rollback incident
- Last reviewed by: Marco Perez on 2026-03-01

Related artifacts and links:
- Pre-rollout checklist template: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/templates/pre-rollout-checklist
- Canary dashboard: /dashboards/canary-health

End of document.
